title: Finite fibre over a point
statement:
Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes and $s\in S$. If $f$ is
locally of finite type and $f^{-1}(\{s\})$ is a finite set, then $X_s$
is a finite discrete space and $f$ is quasi-finite at each point of
$X$ lying over $s$.

proof.text: Choose affine opens $V\cong\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq S$ with $s\in V$ and $U\cong\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq X$ with $f(U)\subseteq V$, and let $\mathfrak p\subset R$ be the prime of $s$. By [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs] $R\to A$ is of finite type, hence so is $\kappa(s)\to A\otimes_R\kappa(s)$ (images of generators generate). Since $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)\to S$ factors through $V$, [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product] and [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] identify the open subscheme $p^{-1}(U)$ of $X_s$ ($p:X_s\to X$ the first projection) with $\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_R\kappa(s))$. By [def-pc-scheme-fibre] $p$ is a homeomorphism of $X_s$ onto $f^{-1}(\{s\})$, which is finite; so $X_s$, and hence $\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_R\kappa(s))$, has finitely many points. By [pqf-lem-finite-type-algebra-finite-spectrum] this spectrum is finite discrete, so every point of the open set $p^{-1}(U)$ is open in $X_s$. Such opens $p^{-1}(U)$ cover $X_s$, so $X_s$ is discrete, and finite as just shown. For a point $x$ over $s$, take such $U\ni x$ and $V$ and apply [lem-weil-pbc-isolated-fibre-point-quasi-finite-affine-pairs] (its hypotheses: $f$ locally of finite type, the point of $X_s$ over $x$ isolated): $R\to A$ is of finite type and quasi-finite at the prime corresponding to $x$, which is exactly the witness required by [pqf-def-quasifinite]. Thus $f$ is quasi-finite at every point lying over $s$.
